riskLevels.title: Three levels, never a percentage.
riskLevels.subtitle: A risk level is not proof: it is a practical guide to help you decide.

low.label: Low risk
low.headline: Few warning signals detected. Contextual information may be missing.
low.action: Keep verifying official terms and verified payment methods.

moderate.label: Caution
moderate.headline: Multiple uncertainties or a notable warning signal identified.
moderate.action: Seek independent verification. Avoid irreversible payment choices.

high.label: High risk
high.headline: Multiple strong signals or critical verification failure.
high.action: Do not rush into paying. Use an official, recognized channel.

limits.title: A tool that is honest about its limits.
limits.subtitle: Good advice also states what it cannot do.
whatWeDoList: Identifies signs of a misleading link, without ever opening it.
Explains warning signals found in a message.
Asks straightforward questions about a transaction.
Guides verification of an unconfirmed payment.
Offers self-assessment guidance after an accidental click.
whatWeDontDoList: It does not prove whether someone is a scammer.
It never guarantees that a link or deal is completely safe.
It does not confirm a payment on your behalf.
It does not remove viruses or scan your phone storage.

commitments.com1Desc: We never ask for your password, PIN code, or OTP verification code.
commitments.com2Desc: Reviewed confidentially by human moderators, never posted automatically.
commitments.com3Desc: We focus on factual warning signals, never personal accusations.

items.question: Can KmerShield tell me if someone is a scammer?
items.answer: No. The application assesses risk based on observable signals. It proves nothing and accuses no one.

items.question: Does “low risk” mean I can pay with zero worries?
items.answer: No. It means few signals were detected, but information may be incomplete. Always continue verifying through official channels.

items.question: Are my links opened by KmerShield?
items.answer: Never. A link is analyzed strictly as plain text: domain spelling, deceptive subdomains, unusual syntax. It is never visited or executed.

items.question: Do you verify my payment for me?
items.answer: No. The application guides you to check your provider’s official transaction history, matching the exact amount and reference ID. A screenshot is never proof.

items.question: What happens to my incident report?
items.answer: Incident reporting is reserved for registered users. You receive a tracking ID, a moderator reviews it privately, and nothing is published automatically. You can follow its status.
